manifest.name: dsh-peak
manifest.description: DeepSeek API peak/off-peak pricing indicator: a live composer pill (red during peak, green off-peak) with a countdown to the next switch and the weekend/Chinese-holiday off-peak rules, plus a dsh_peak_status tool the agent can call to warn about cost.

bundle.text:
# dsh-peak bundle patch: mounts the peak/off-peak pricing indicator.
#
# Applied after the profile's base layer. The row's `name` is this package
# itself: the loader imports the package entry (the host half, which registers
# the dsh_peak_status tool), and the package's `dsh.client` declaration makes
# the client-modules service serve /plugins/dsh-peak/client.js so the browser
# half (the composer pill) mounts in every session.

- insert:
    - id: dsh-peak
      name: 'dsh-peak'

readme.text:
A live **peak/off-peak pricing indicator** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), shipped as an installable dual-face bundle.

DeepSeek's API moved to peak/off-peak pricing on **2026-08-16 16:00 UTC**: during peak windows the rate is **2× the off-peak rate**, and the windows line up almost exactly with Chinese work hours. Weekends and Chinese statutory holidays are billed off-peak **all day**. This plugin makes that visible:

- **Composer pill** (browser): a small always-visible control at the left of the input row — **red "PEAK"** during peak windows, **green "OFF-PEAK"** otherwise, with a live countdown to the next switch and a hover tooltip showing UTC + Beijing times and the reason the day is off-peak.
- **`dsh_peak_status` tool** (host): the agent can call it before suggesting or running long/expensive work, so it can warn you when you're about to pay the peak rate.

Peak applies on days that are neither a weekend nor a Chinese statutory holiday:

| Window | Beijing | UTC |
|---|---|---|
| Peak 1 | 09:00–12:00 weekdays | 01:00–04:00 |
| Peak 2 | 14:00–18:00 weekdays | 06:00–10:00 |
| Off-peak | everything else | — (half of peak) |

Whole-day off-peak, since **2026-08-23 00:00 Beijing**:

| Day | Rule |
|---|---|
| Saturday + Sunday | off-peak all day, including make-up workdays (调休) that fall on a weekend |
| Chinese statutory holidays | off-peak all day (DeepSeek notice of 2026-09-19) |

Holidays follow the State Council's annual arrangement ([国办发明电〔2025〕7号](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202511/content_7047091.htm)). The 2026 table covers Mid-Autumn (Sep 25) and National Day (Oct 1–7), which — with the Sep 20 and Oct 10 make-up weekends — make Sep 20 to Oct 10, 2026 almost entirely off-peak.

`core.js` holds the whole-day rules: `HOLIDAYS` (inclusive Beijing date ranges, listed only from the 2026-09-19 notice onward), `MAKEUP_WORKDAYS` (labels only — a make-up workday is off-peak because it is a weekend), and `HOLIDAY_CALENDAR_THROUGH`, the last date the table covers. The State Council publishes the next year's arrangement each November, so update all three when it lands; until then the tool appends a warning to its summary and the pill's tooltip, because holidays after that date would be misreported as peak.

Both halves run the same code: `index.js` imports `core.js`, while the browser bundle embeds the marked region from `core.js` verbatim (a bundle is served as one script and cannot import a sibling module).

- A DeepSeek Harness **web profile** (the pill mounts in the browser; the tool registers host-side)
- No runtime dependencies — the host half uses a raw `ctx.tools.register` definition and the client bundle's only external is `react`

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-peak            # once published to npm
dsh plugin --profile web add github:geokkjer/dsh-peak   # or straight from this repo
```

Or from a local checkout of this repo:

```sh
cd /path/to/dsh-peak
dsh plugin --profile web add .
```

`dsh plugin` runs `pnpm add` in the profile directory and registers the package as a bundle layer (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`). After the next `dsh web` restart, both halves activate: the host row registers `dsh_peak_status`, and the `dsh.client` declaration makes the browser roster serve `/plugins/dsh-peak/client.js`, mounting the pill in every session.

Ask the agent:

- *"is it peak pricing right now?"* → calls `dsh_peak_status`
- *"run this long job off-peak"* → the agent checks `dsh_peak_status` first and reports the window

The pill itself needs no interaction: it self-updates every 30s and flips color at each window boundary.

`dsh_peak_status` returns the `summary` an agent reads plus structured fields: `peak`, `offPeakReason` (`weekend` / `holiday` / `none`, the last when only the peak-window rule applies), `holidayName` (empty unless the day is a holiday), `makeupWorkday`, the UTC and Beijing clocks, `nextSwitchUtc` / `nextSwitchInMinutes`, and `holidayCalendarThrough` / `holidayCalendarStale`.

Tool schemas use the harness's JSON-schema subset, which takes a single `type` string per node — a `type` array disables the whole plugin entry at load, so `offPeakReason` carries the `none` sentinel instead of a nullable type.

The repo is deliberately build-free: `core.js`, `index.js` (host tool), and `client.js` (browser bundle in the module-loader format) are committed plain ESM, so `pnpm add` works with no `prepare` step.

```sh
npm run sync:client   # after editing core.js: refresh the region embedded in client.js
npm test
```

`npm test` runs the smoke suite: host identity + tool registration, window and whole-day classification at known instants (09:46 UTC → peak; 05:00 UTC → off-peak; Mid-Autumn and National Day → off-peak all day, including the switch that skips the whole National Day break; make-up workday weekends), a check that `client.js` still embeds the current `core.js`, and client bundle materialization against a stubbed module loader + React.
